heading: Okanagan Cideries for Apple Season
title: Okanagan Cideries: An Apple-Season Guide | Okanagan Roam
description: Orchard cideries, cider with a proper meal, family- and dog-friendly tasting rooms and tours that do the driving, from Osoyoos to Enderby.
intro: Apple season is a natural time to taste Okanagan cider. Many of the valley's cideries press fruit from their own orchards, and several pair a flight with a real kitchen, lawn games for the kids or a spot for the dog.

Some tasting rooms are seasonal, so check hours before you go. The {event:lake-country/lake-country-cider-fest|Lake Country Cider Fest} is listed for October 17 and 18 on the Lake Country Cider Trail; confirm details with the organizer before you go.

sections.heading: Cider from the orchard outside the door

items.name: Creek & Gully Cider
items.text: Naramata Bench cider made from certified-organic apples grown right outside the tasting room. Take a flight of crisp, dry ciders onto the orchard patio and look out over the trees they came from.

items.name: Orchard Hill Estate Cidery
items.text: One of BC's original estate cideries, pouring apple ciders from its own South Okanagan orchards on the highway between Oliver and Osoyoos. Open seasonally, mid-May through October.

items.name: Tony's Craft Cidery
items.text: Small-batch ciders on a cozy tasting-room porch, out among 50 acres of apple and cherry trees in Lavington. Pair a flight with something from the seasonal menu. It's an easy, scenic detour on the road from Vernon to Lumby.

items.name: Rose Hill Orchard & Cidery
items.text: Pick your own cherries, peaches or apples, then trade the bucket for a cider flight under the trees. A working orchard with a farm shop and picnic tables.

items.name: NOMAD Cider
items.text: A small farm-to-glass cidery on Bottleneck Drive making low-intervention ciders from fresh-pressed Okanagan apples and pears. Its wild-fermented ciders take cues from England, France, Spain, Germany and Quebec, and the picnic area under the walnut trees looks out to Giant's Head Mountain.

items.name: Cambium Cider Co
items.text: An orchard cidery paired with a genuine restaurant, so a quick stop can turn into a full afternoon. Order beyond a flight, because the kitchen is worth exploring too. Dogs aren't allowed inside or on the patio, but leashed dogs are welcome at a few picnic tables in the orchard.

items.name: Farmstrong Cider Company
items.text: A menu that changes often, wood-fired pizzas reviewers call standout, and board games at the table for anyone who wants to linger.

items.name: Upside Cidery
items.text: A big, lively cidery with lawn and upstairs patio seating, wood-fired pizza and real non-alcoholic options.

items.name: Ricardo's at Soma
items.text: Chef Ricardo's Italian-leaning plates with Soma's craft ciders on an orchard patio in southeast Kelowna. A relaxed spot to linger over a flight and a shared board. Open seasonally, Thursday to Sunday.

items.name: Folktale Cider
items.text: A trampoline, zipline, chicken coop and cider-and-wine slushies. A rare cider stop where kids have as much to do as the adults.

items.name: Millionaires' Row Cider Co.
items.text: A family-run cidery on a historic orchard, with a picnic area, board games and apple slushies for the kids.

items.name: Truck 59 Ciderhouse
items.text: An orchard cidery with a family-and-dog-friendly main lawn, lawn games and a separate adults-only lounge.

items.name: Summerland Heritage Cider Company
items.text: A "bark board" built for visiting dogs, and complimentary slushies for the humans.

items.name: Scenic Road Cider Co.
items.text: An award-winning cidery in a 100-year-old heritage building, with a picnic area where you can bring your own food to go with the tastings.

items.name: Dominion Cider Co.
items.text: Dry, fruit-forward bottles, plus custom-label cans for events. A cidery for people who want something beyond the standard sweet apple can.

items.name: Shuswap Cider Company
items.text: A small craft cidery run by two women on a farm beside the Shuswap River. The ciders use BC apples plus fruit and botanicals from the farm and the Shuswap area, poured as flights and on tap, with a dog-friendly patio.

items.name: Liber Farms & Winery
items.text: A small winery just off Highway 97 with a beautiful patio and homemade apple juice and cider.

items.name: The View Winery & Vineyard
items.text: A smaller winery with its own on-site cidery, so you can try cider alongside the wine, and live music on the patio.

sections.heading: Let someone else drive, or taste at the market

items.name: Top Cat Tours
items.text: Running since 2001, with daily shared and private tours and door-to-door pickup. Options include beer, cider and distillery tours. Season: March to November.

items.name: Signature Connections (formerly Kelowna Concierge)
items.text: A long-running tour and shuttle company whose "Sip and Sample" tour takes in craft breweries, distilleries and cideries.

items.name: Pedego Electric Bikes Oyama
items.text: E-bike rentals from Gatzke's Farm Market, right beside the Okanagan Rail Trail between Wood and Kalamalka lakes. Partner tours pair a ride with wine or cider tastings; riders must be 16 and up.

items.name: Penticton Farmers' Market
items.text: Every Saturday morning from mid-April to the end of October on the 100 block of Main Street. Among more than 90 vendors, local wineries, cideries and breweries offer samples.
